tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. Every step runs even if an earlier one fails; the result lists each step. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Requests cancellation of one running background job; the hardware operation is stopped where possible (exposure aborted, slew stopped, focuser halted, autofocus aborted). Waits up to wait_seconds (default 10) for the job to end and returns it in the get_job shape, with stopErrors listing driver stop commands that failed. Cancelling a job that already finished is not an error. If the job is still running after the wait (its device does not respond), abandon: true releases its resource anyway; the device may still be busy, so check get_status afterwards. Available even in read-only mode and while a sequence runs. To stop everything at once use stop_all.

tools.name: capture_image

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. tools.name: get_sequence
tools.description: The sequence currently loaded in the advanced sequencer as a tree: each node has path (index path such as "1/0/2"), name, type, status (Created, Running, Finished, Failed, Skipped, Disabled), details (e.g. target coordinates, exposure time, filter, progress) and children. Also tells whether it is running. Use it to inspect a loaded sequence before start_sequence and to follow progress (which target and exposure block is active). notes flags targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

max_depth.description: Maximum tree depth to return (1-10, default 4); deeper nodes are omitted.

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: add_target

Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: get_recent_images
tools.description: The newest entries of the image history (captures by the sequence and by capture_image), newest first: time, image type, filter, exposure in seconds, HFR (half flux radius in pixels, lower is sharper), detected star count, mean/median/standard deviation in ADU, camera temperature in °C, guiding RMS in arcsec, target name and file path, and for saved frames FWHM in pixels, eccentricity and the focuser position. get_session_summary aggregates them. Use it to judge focus (rising HFR → run_autofocus), clouds (star count drops), and sequence progress.

tools.name: list_target_templates
tools.description: Names of the saved target templates (deep sky object containers prepared by the user with their preferred instructions: centering, autofocus triggers, exposure blocks, dithering). Pass one as 'template' to add_target to reuse the user's own imaging recipe instead of building an exposure plan.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Requests cancellation of one running background job; the hardware operation is stopped where possible (exposure aborted, slew stopped, focuser halted, autofocus aborted). Waits up to wait_seconds (default 10) for the job to end and returns it in the get_job shape, with stopErrors listing driver stop commands that failed. Cancelling a job that already finished is not an error. If the job is still running after the wait (its device does not respond), abandon: true releases its resource anyway; the device may still be busy, so check get_status afterwards. Available even in read-only mode and while a sequence runs. To stop everything at once use stop_all.

job_id.description: Id of the job to cancel, e.g. "job-7f3a2c".

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the job to end after the cancel request (0-55, default 10).

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. Every step runs even if an earlier one fails; the result lists each step. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. Every step runs even if an earlier one fails; the result lists each step. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. tools.name: capture_image

(2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: add_target

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: get_sequence
tools.description: The sequence currently loaded in the advanced sequencer as a tree: each node has path (index path such as "1/0/2"), name, type, status (Created, Running, Finished, Failed, Skipped, Disabled), details (e.g. target coordinates, exposure time, filter, progress) and children. Also tells whether it is running. Use it to inspect a loaded sequence before start_sequence and to follow progress (which target and exposure block is active). notes flags targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

max_depth.description: Maximum tree depth to return (1-10, default 4); deeper nodes are omitted.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Requests cancellation of one running background job; the hardware operation is stopped where possible (exposure aborted, slew stopped, focuser halted, autofocus aborted). Waits up to wait_seconds (default 10) for the job to end and returns it in the get_job shape, with stopErrors listing driver stop commands that failed. Cancelling a job that already finished is not an error. If the job is still running after the wait (its device does not respond), abandon: true releases its resource anyway; the device may still be busy, so check get_status afterwards. Available even in read-only mode and while a sequence runs. To stop everything at once use stop_all.

job_id.description: Id of the job to cancel, e.g. "job-7f3a2c".

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the job to end after the cancel request (0-55, default 10).

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. Every step runs even if an earlier one fails; the result lists each step. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

Claims no resource, so it also works while a start_guiding job is still calibrating (cancel that job with cancel_job to abort the start instead). While a sequence runs it needs force, because stopping guiding spoils the sequence's exposures.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: start_guiding
tools.description: Starts autoguiding with the connected guider (selects a guide star, calibrates if needed, then guides). The mount must track. Calibration can take a few minutes, so this may return a running job: poll get_job. Afterwards watch guider state and RMS (arcsec) in get_status; get_guider_report has the details. Refused while a mount job (slew, park, home, centering) runs. A sequence built with add_target starts guiding by itself.

force_calibration.description: Discard the existing calibration and calibrate again (after changing the guide setup or a large declination change). Default false.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

Also tells whether it is running. Use it to inspect a loaded sequence before start_sequence and to follow progress (which target and exposure block is active). notes flags targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

max_depth.description: Maximum tree depth to return (1-10, default 4); deeper nodes are omitted.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: cancel_job

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

The mount must be connected and unparked (unpark_mount). Moves the telescope: make sure the user expects it. If guiding is active, stop_guiding first (the guide star is lost during the slew). Runs as a background job holding the mount; refused while a capture, autofocus or guiding start job runs. Stop it with cancel_job or stop_all. Afterwards check the position with get_status.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: park_mount

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. Every step runs even if an earlier one fails; the result lists each step. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: stop_sequence
tools.description: Stops the running advanced sequence (the current instruction is interrupted, e.g. the exposure is aborted). Does not park the mount, stop guiding or warm the camera. Progress is kept: start_sequence continues with unfinished items, reset_sequence starts over. Safe to call when nothing runs. Never refused by the sequence guard.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: list_target_templates
tools.description: Names of the saved target templates (deep sky object containers prepared by the user with their preferred instructions: centering, autofocus triggers, exposure blocks, dithering). Pass one as 'template' to add_target to reuse the user's own imaging recipe instead of building an exposure plan.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: get_recent_images
tools.description: The newest entries of the image history (captures by the sequence and by capture_image), newest first: time, image type, filter, exposure in seconds, HFR (half flux radius in pixels, lower is sharper), detected star count, mean/median/standard deviation in ADU, camera temperature in °C, guiding RMS in arcsec, target name and file path, and for saved frames FWHM in pixels, eccentricity and the focuser position. get_session_summary aggregates them. Use it to judge focus (rising HFR → run_autofocus), clouds (star count drops), and sequence progress.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: stop_sequence
tools.description: Stops the running advanced sequence (the current instruction is interrupted, e.g. the exposure is aborted). Does not park the mount, stop guiding or warm the camera. Progress is kept: start_sequence continues with unfinished items, reset_sequence starts over. Safe to call when nothing runs. Never refused by the sequence guard.

tools.name: add_target

Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: add_target

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: start_sequence

tools.name: capture_image

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Starts the advanced sequence that is loaded (load_sequence) or built (add_target) and returns as soon as it runs; it then runs on its own for hours, moving the mount, camera, focuser and guider. NINA validates the sequence first (devices connected, filters exist, ...) and refuses with the issues listed; skip_validation bypasses that check (not recommended). While it runs, other hardware and change tools are refused unless force is passed. Monitor with get_status, get_sequence and get_recent_images; stop with stop_sequence (or stop_all). Finished items are skipped on a new start: reset_sequence first to run everything again. Refused while a job started over MCP (slew, capture, autofocus, focuser move, filter change, guiding start, switch, device connection) still runs: wait for it with get_job or stop it with cancel_job. A running camera cooling job does not block the start. The result notes targets that no meridian flip trigger covers.

tools.name: stop_all
tools.description: Emergency stop. In this order: stops the advanced sequence (so it cannot start its next item), cancels every background job, aborts the running camera exposure, stops the mount if it is slewing and halts a focuser move started over MCP. It does NOT park the mount, stop guiding, warm the camera or disconnect anything; an idle mount is left alone (note that aborting a slew stops tracking on some mount drivers); a dome shutter that is closing keeps closing. Safe to repeat. Use it whenever the user says stop/abort or something looks wrong (unexpected movement, collision risk, clouds/rain). This tool is never refused: together with cancel_job it stays available in read-only mode, and it needs no force while a sequence runs. Afterwards check get_status.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. tools.name: run_autofocus

tools.name: capture_image
tools.description: Takes one exposure with the imaging camera (changing the filter first when 'filter' is set) and returns its statistics in outcome.data (HFR in pixels, star count, mean/median ADU). The frame is also added to the image history (get_recent_images). Use it for test frames: framing, focus check, exposure check. By default the frame is analysed but not saved; save: true writes it like a normal LIGHT frame (the file path appears in get_recent_images once it is written). Omitted gain/offset use the profile defaults; omitted binning keeps the camera's current binning. Runs as a background job holding the camera and refused while a focuser move, filter change or mount job (slew, park, home, centering), rotator move or flat device job runs; the default wait covers short exposures, poll get_job for long ones. For many frames build a sequence with add_target instead.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel (see get_status), e.g. "Ha" or "L". Omit to keep the current filter.

gain.description: Camera gain (driver units). Omit for the profile default gain.

offset.description: Camera offset (driver units). Omit for the profile default offset.

binning.description: Symmetric binning factor (1-4; 2 = 2x2). Omit to keep the current binning.

save.description: Save the frame to disk as a LIGHT frame. Default false (snapshot, analysed only).

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the operation to finish before returning (0-55, default 30). If it is still running, the result holds the job id: poll get_job. The operation continues in the background either way.

tools.name: add_target
tools.description: Adds an imaging target to the end of the advanced sequence's target area. Two ways, pass exactly one: (1) 'template': a saved target template (list_target_templates) whose target name and coordinates are replaced; the template's own instructions are used and the plan options below are not allowed. (2) 'exposures': an exposure plan; pins builds the target from standard instructions in this order: slew and center with plate solving (slew_and_center, default true), autofocus (autofocus_at_start, default false), start guiding (start_guiding, default true), then one exposure block per entry (filter, exposure, count, gain/offset/binning, dithering every dither_every frames), with NINA's meridian flip trigger on the target (meridian_flip, default true; settings from the profile) so that a German equatorial mount flips instead of tracking into the pier. Coordinates are J2000. Only edits the sequence (nothing moves); check the result with get_sequence, then start_sequence. Adding while the sequence runs needs force.

name.description: Target name used for the sequence container and file names, e.g. "M 42".

rotation_degrees.description: Desired sky position angle of the camera in degrees (0 <= x < 360), used by slew-and-center with a rotator. Omit to keep the default.

template.description: Name of a saved target template (list_target_templates). Mutually exclusive with exposures.

exposures.description: Exposure plan: one block per entry, executed in order. Mutually exclusive with template.

exposure_seconds.description: Exposure time of each frame in seconds (0.0001-3600).

filter.description: Filter name as configured in the filter wheel, e.g. "Ha". Omit for no filter change.

gain.description: Camera gain. Omit for the profile default.

offset.description: Camera offset. Omit for the profile default.

binning.description: Symmetric binning (1-4). Omit for 1x1 / profile default.

slew_and_center.description: Exposure plan only: slew, plate solve and center (and rotate) before imaging. Default true.

start_guiding.description: Exposure plan only: start guiding before the exposures. Default true.

autofocus_at_start.description: Exposure plan only: run autofocus after centering. Default false.

dither_every.description: Exposure plan only: dither after every N frames (0 = never, max 32 like NINA). Default 0.

meridian_flip.description: Exposure plan only: add NINA's meridian flip trigger to the target. Default true; turn off for fork mounts.
